label: prf:wedderburn-mass-formula
title: Proof of wedderburn mass formula
html:
Proof. Work over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] at generic q, passing to the fraction field where inverses are required; write h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} for the Hecke parameter and z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) (convention D) for the Markov weight, so that the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is the linear functional normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z (positive stabilisation).

Step 1 — extremal Wedderburn blocks and channel eigenvalues. By the three-parameter decomposition, H_3(R, q) \cong M_1(R) \oplus M_2(R) \oplus M_1(R), with blocks labelled by the partitions (3), (2,1), (1,1,1); for general n the corresponding extremal blocks are the symmetric [n], standard [n-1, 1], and alternating [1^n] representations. The Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 gives each generator the eigenvalue q in the symmetric channel and -q^{-1} in the alternating channel; since all \sigma_i are conjugate, the two one-dimensional blocks are the algebra characters \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(\sigma_i) = q and \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(\sigma_i) = -q^{-1}. A typed crossing element X = c \cdot \sigma_i + d \cdot \mathbf{1} (transfer matrix) therefore evaluates in the two scalar channels as

\lambda^{\mathrm{sym}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(X) = cq + d,
\qquad
\lambda^{\mathrm{alt}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(X)
  = -c q^{-1} + d .

Step 2 — the transfer matrix is the regular representation of the crossing algebra. A single crossing generates the two-dimensional commutative algebra R[\sigma] = R[x] / \bigl((x - q)(x + q^{-1})\bigr), in which \sigma^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} \sigma + 1. In the ordered basis (\sigma, 1), multiplication by X = c\sigma + d has matrix exactly the crossing (transfer) matrix of the statement,

T(X) =
\begin{pmatrix}
  c h_{\mathrm{A}} + d & c \\
  c & d
\end{pmatrix},

since X \cdot \sigma = c\sigma^2 + d\sigma = (ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d)\,\sigma + c and X \cdot 1 = c\sigma + d. As a matrix of left multiplication, T is an algebra homomorphism: T(X)\,T(X') = T(XX'), which one verifies directly — XX' = c''\sigma + d'' with c'' = cc'h_{\mathrm{A}} + cd' + c'd and d'' = cc' + dd', matching the entries of the matrix product. Consequently, for the chained element X_i := \prod_{j > i} X_j of the crossings of all strands j > i, the transfer-matrix chain satisfies M_i = \prod_{j > i} T(X_j) = T(X_i), and reading off the basis coefficients gives (M_i)_{12} = (M_i)_{21} = c_i and (M_i)_{22} = d_i, where X_i = c_i \sigma + d_i. Moreover the eigenvalues of M_i = T(X_i) are precisely the two character values \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i) and \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i), since the regular representation of R[\sigma] diagonalises along its two characters. (Chaining within a single crossing algebra is the defining Level-0 transfer-matrix reduction; the exact all-partitions computation replaces it for n \ge 4, as the statement records.)

Step 3 — the three invariants are the three extremal block readouts.

  1. Markov trace (standard block). By linearity and the normalisation above, \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i) = c_i\,z + d_i = z\,(M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}. Hence \Phi_1 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert z\,(M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}\bigr\rvert = \sum_i \ln\lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i)\rvert is the Markov-weighted trace datum of the chain — the invariant attached to the standard (dim n{-}1) block in the correspondence table.
  2. Determinant = sym \times alt. Directly, \det T(X) = (ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d)\,d - c^2 = cdh_{\mathrm{A}} + d^2 - c^2 = (cq + d)(-cq^{-1} + d) = \lambda^{\mathrm{sym}}\lambda^{\mathrm{alt}}; equivalently this is the product of the two eigenvalues exhibited in Step 2. By multiplicativity of the determinant and of the characters, \det M_i = \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\,\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}, so \Phi_2 = \sum_i \bigl(\ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert + \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert\bigr).
  3. Ratio = sym / alt (chirality). \Phi_3 = \sum_i \bigl(\ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert - \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert\bigr).

From 2 and 3, \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert and \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert are recovered as half the sum and half the difference of the per-chain summands: the pair (\Phi_2, \Phi_3) is an invertible linear repackaging of the two one-dimensional block evaluations, while \Phi_1 carries the standard-block Markov datum. The triple (\Phi_1, \Phi_2, \Phi_3) therefore carries exactly the evaluations of the three extremal Wedderburn blocks on the chain — no more and no fewer. This is the claimed completeness at the 2 \times 2 transfer level: the chain data (c_i, d_i) \in R^2 of the two-dimensional crossing algebra support precisely the two characters and the Markov functional exhibited, and every block-respecting multiplicative invariant of \{M_i\} is a function of these three. For n \ge 4 the non-extremal partitions contribute additional invariants, computed exactly by the full partition sum via Young's seminormal form, as stated.

Step 4 — the coefficients. The overall scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the archimedean evaluation of the algebraic binding scale m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_3), with \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G the Borromean volume (binding scale). The determinant weight \beta_2 = -2[3]_q is the degree-two baryon weight (degree-2 weight): the three color channels give the pair count \binom{3}{2} = 3, q-deformed to [3]_q, with the sign fixed by the determinant sign accumulation and the factor 2 by the \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n} crossing-doubling convention established there. The chirality weight h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 is the minimal even power of the Hecke parameter compatible with the S-parity classification of the three terms (S-classification) and with the vanishing of the chirality contribution in the commutative limit (commutative chirality): h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 as q \to 1, so h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \to 0 and the classical mass formula retains no chirality term. All three weights are functions of q alone, evaluated at q_0, and the scale is fixed by m_e: no fitted parameter enters.

Assembling: the binding functional \alpha\,(\Phi_1 - 2[3]_q\,\Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3) is the weighted sum of the three extremal-block invariants of the atomic braid established in Steps 1–3, with the weights of Step 4, added to the free constituent masses Z \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z \cdot m_e. \square

The numerical agreement of this formula with measured atomic masses across the nuclide table is an empirical cross-check, not part of the proof; the certifying witness previously cited here (atom-mass-complete-wedderburn.witness.json) is absent from computations/ and its regeneration is tracked as an open follow-up.
